summary:
Silt-Watch is an Earth observation analysis tool that detects hidden storage capacity loss in dams and reservoirs caused by gradual sediment buildup. Even when a reservoir looks full from above, upstream soil erosion quietly fills the dam bed with silt over time—reducing its actual water-holding depth and increasing the risk of summer water shortages and monsoon floods.
Acting as a hydrological trend detective, Silt-Watch cross-references 12 years of NASA GPM rainfall data against Landsat 8/9 surface water measurements (NDWI) and MODIS vegetation indices. Using time-series linear regression, it identifies reservoirs where dry-season water retention is shrinking steadily despite consistent annual rainfall. By isolating siltation from temporary drought conditions, Silt-Watch gives irrigation boards and local planners a low-cost early warning system to prioritize desilting operations without relying solely on expensive sonar surveys.
details:
Silt-Watch is an Earth observation analysis tool that detects hidden storage capacity loss in dams and reservoirs caused by gradual sediment buildup. Even when a reservoir looks full from above, upstream soil erosion quietly fills the dam bed with silt over time, reducing its actual water-holding depth and increasing the risk of summer water shortages and monsoon floods.

How it works: Acting as a hydrological trend detective, Silt-Watch cross-references 12 years of NASA GPM rainfall data against Landsat 8/9 surface water measurements (NDWI) and MODIS vegetation indices. Using time-series linear regression, it identifies reservoirs where dry-season water retention is shrinking steadily despite consistent annual rainfall. This method isolates siltation from temporary drought conditions.

Benefits and Impact: It gives irrigation boards and local planners a low-cost early warning system to prioritize desilting operations without relying solely on expensive sonar surveys. This helps prevent water shortages, improves flood management, and protects farmers and local communities.

Tools Used: NASA GPM, Landsat 8/9, MODIS, Google Earth Engine concept, NDWI analysis, time-series linear regression, and Google Slides / Canva for visualization.

Creativity and Factors Considered: Instead of looking at a single satellite image, we looked at 12 years of trends. We considered rainfall variation, vegetation change, seasonal water levels, and local needs of Kerala and India where dams are critical for drinking water, farming, and flood control.
